newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norsk Hydro said to mull fish-farm spinoff.
newsitem.headline: Norsk Hydro said to mull fish-farm spinoff.

text.p: Norwegian industrial giant Norsk Hydro ASA may spin off its Hydro Seafood division and list it separately on the Oslo bourse, the daily financial Dagens Naeringsliv (DN) said on Friday.
Hydro Seafood is the world's leading salmon farmer but Norsk Hydro's management has never hidden the fact that its seafood activities were not among the company's core interests, DN said.

"The last few years there has been much speculation over if and when Hydro will get out of fish farming. Instead of selling out there has been a lot of buying of other companies in the same branch, such that Hydro Seafood has grown strongly and is now the world's largest player in the field," the newspaper said.
Turnover for the division in 1996 amounted to 1.5 billion crowns ($212.7 million), but following recent acquisitions turnover is now around two billion crowns per year despite lower prices, it said.
It added that Hydro Seafood is too big to be sold to a single buyer and in any case too big to be bought by a competitor company.
"We have considered whether we should list Hydro Seafood on the Oslo bourse. That is one possibility, but it is not today an actuality," Hydro Seafood spokesman Odd Gullberg told DN.
"The focus is now on the group's development. We have changed management and bought many companies, and now we need to get everything working effectively after the large expansion."
Gullberg said Hydro Seafood had to reduce costs and consolidate operations to remain profitable while prices are low and margins squeezed.
One of the measures had been to establish Hydro Seafood Sales to centralise marketing of its products from the Shetlands, Ireland, Scotland and Norway, he said.
DN said one analyst put the unit's market value on the Oslo bourse at one billion crowns.
